title: API Gateway: REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs

videos.script: A function on its own has no address. Somebody has to stand at the door, take the request and hand it over. On AWS that is usually API Gateway. {{door}} It comes in three kinds, and this lesson builds all three against moto. The REST API is the oldest. You build a tree of paths and verbs, and nothing answers until you take a deployment and put it on a stage. It is also the one with API keys, usage plans and a cache. {{tree}} The HTTP API is newer and smaller. One route is a method and a path. It deploys itself, it checks a token for you, and it costs well under half as much per request. You will run its handler in the real Lambda runtime, with the event it would receive. {{route}} The WebSocket API keeps a connection open, so the server can speak first. It bills twice: once per message, once per minute connected. You will work out when that beats asking every five seconds. {{socket}} moto keeps every definition, but it serves nothing at an API's address. So no request in this lesson meets a key check, a token or a throttle. Where that matters, the lesson says what AWS does instead. {{choose}} And at the end, a way to choose: the HTTP API, unless you can name the feature that needs the other one.
